---
title: "Cellular communities in bone-marrow samples"
author: "LazDaria, ArthurDondi"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  workflowr::wflow_html
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: inline
params:
  input: !r Sys.getenv("MAPMET2_INPUT", "/mnt/data/input_all")
  output: !r Sys.getenv("MAPMET2_OUTPUT", "/mnt/data/output_mapmet2")
  # TRUE: all BM samples incl. the normal control BM; FALSE: NB-patient samples only
  include_controls: TRUE
  # Composition the samples are clustered on: "all" (all cell types),
  # "immune" (immune cell types, within the immune cells) or "tcell" (T-cell
  # types, within the cells of the "T cells" metacluster)
  cluster_on: "all"
  # Number of communities cut from the sample dendrogram, or "auto" (the largest
  # k whose communities are all bootstrap-stable, see "Number of communities")
  n_communities: "auto"
  # k values compared in "Number of communities": 2..k_max
  k_max: 8
  # Bootstrap resamples for the cluster stability (Jaccard)
  n_boot: 100
  # Samples with fewer cells are left out (their composition is too noisy)
  min_cells: 100
  # ... and, for cluster_on = "immune" / "tcell", samples with fewer cells in that compartment
  min_cells_compartment: 10
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
variant  <- paste0(params$cluster_on, "_", if (isTRUE(params$include_controls)) "with_controls" else "without_controls")
plot_dir <- file.path(params$output, "plots/05.1_BM_cellularcomm", variant)
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) {
  dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

date_prefix <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")

# Save a plot (ggplot / patchwork / grob) as PDF or PNG, by file extension
save_plot <- function(plot_obj, filename, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  full_path <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(date_prefix, "_", filename))
  if (inherits(plot_obj, "ggplot")) {
    ggsave(full_path, plot = plot_obj, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi,
           bg = "white", limitsize = FALSE)
  } else {
    if (grepl("\\.png$", full_path)) png(full_path, width = width, height = height, units = "in", res = dpi)
    else pdf(full_path, width = width, height = height)
    grid::grid.draw(plot_obj)
    dev.off()
  }
  message("Saved: ", full_path)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  dev = "png",
  dpi = 300,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 6
)
```

# Cellular communities in bone-marrow samples {#bm-cellularcomm}

Adapted from MapMetSC's `05.1_PT_DE_cellularcomm.Rmd`, which clusters diagnostic primary tumors on their tumor cell-type composition. Here we cluster **bone-marrow samples** on the composition of `r c(all = "**all their cell types**", immune = "their **immune cell types** (within the immune cells)", tcell = "their **T-cell types** (within the T cells)")[[params$cluster_on]]`. This report is the variant **`r variant`**: `r if (isTRUE(params$include_controls)) "all BM samples, including the normal control BM" else "the NB-patient BM samples only (DE, T1, T2, REL), without the normal control BM"`.

The combined figures stack the sample dendrogram, the composition used for the clustering, the BM sample type (timepoint), the community, the patient-level genetic / clinical tracks, the age at diagnosis and the tumor / immune heterogeneity (Shannon entropy), and the tumor, immune and metacluster compositions (clustered on immune or T-cell types, the all-cell-type composition replaces the immune one, so every variant has the same panels); a second version groups the samples by BM sample type and orders them by clustering within each group.

## Load libraries
<details>
   <summary>Load libraries</summary>

```{r load-libraries}
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggdendro)
library(patchwork)
library(cluster)
```
</details>

## Read data
We load the phenotyped single-cell data from [chapter 4](04_phenotyping.html) and keep one row per cell with its sample (`fm_id`) and the sample- and patient-level metadata.

```{r read-data}
spe <- readRDS(file.path(params$output, "spe_04_phenotyping.rds"))

for (mapmet_cc_path in c("analysis/00_MapMet_color_code.R", "00_MapMet_color_code.R", "../analysis/00_MapMet_color_code.R"))
  if (file.exists(mapmet_cc_path)) { source(mapmet_cc_path); break }

col_celltype    <- metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_celltype_ordered
col_metacluster <- metadata(spe)$color_vectors$col_metacluster
ct_levels       <- levels(spe$celltype_ordered)

cells <- as.data.frame(colData(spe))[, c("fm_id", "patient_id", "timepoint", "celltype", "metacluster",
                                         "MYCN_amp", "X1p_loss", "progression", "age_diag")]
cells$celltype <- factor(as.character(cells$celltype), levels = ct_levels)
if (!isTRUE(params$include_controls)) cells <- cells[cells$timepoint != "control", ]
rm(spe); invisible(gc())

# Immune compartment (as in MapMetSC: not tumor, mesenchymal or other)
immune_meta <- setdiff(unique(as.character(cells$metacluster)), c("tumor", "mesenchymal", "other", NA))

# T cells: the metacluster named "T cells" (matched ignoring case / punctuation / plural)
tcell_meta <- unique(as.character(cells$metacluster))
tcell_meta <- tcell_meta[!is.na(tcell_meta) & norm_label(tcell_meta) == "tcell"]

# Compartment the samples are clustered on (NULL = all cells)
stopifnot(params$cluster_on %in% c("all", "immune", "tcell"))
clust_meta <- switch(params$cluster_on, all = NULL, immune = immune_meta, tcell = tcell_meta)
if (params$cluster_on == "tcell" && !length(clust_meta))
  stop("cluster_on = \"tcell\": no metacluster named \"T cells\" in the annotation.")

# Samples with too few cells (or cells of the clustering compartment) are left out
n_per_sample <- table(cells$fm_id)
too_small    <- names(n_per_sample)[n_per_sample < params$min_cells]
if (!is.null(clust_meta)) {
  n_comp <- table(factor(cells$fm_id[cells$metacluster %in% clust_meta], levels = names(n_per_sample)))
  too_small <- union(too_small, names(n_comp)[n_comp < params$min_cells_compartment])
}
if (length(too_small))
  message(length(too_small), " sample(s) left out (too few cells): ", paste(too_small, collapse = ", "))
cells <- cells[!cells$fm_id %in% too_small, ]
```

The data contain `r length(unique(cells$fm_id))` samples (`r length(too_small)` left out with too few cells).

## Sample-level metadata

```{r sample-metadata}
# MYCN / 1p loss / progression -> yes / no / het (NA for the controls)
recode_ynh <- function(x) dplyr::recode(as.character(x),
  "1" = "yes", "0" = "no", "2" = "het", "9" = "NA",
  "MNA" = "yes", "nMNA" = "no", "het" = "het", "unknown" = "NA",
  "Prog" = "yes", "NoProg" = "no", "yes" = "yes", "no" = "no",
  .default = "NA", .missing = "NA")

# Shannon entropy of a composition (heterogeneity)
shannon <- function(n) { p <- n[n > 0] / sum(n); if (!length(p)) NA_real_ else -sum(p * log(p)) }

samples <- cells %>%
  group_by(fm_id) %>%
  summarise(
    patient_id = first(patient_id),
    timepoint  = first(timepoint),
    mycn       = recode_ynh(first(MYCN_amp)),
    loss1p     = recode_ynh(first(X1p_loss)),
    prog       = recode_ynh(first(progression)),
    age_diag   = as.numeric(first(age_diag)),
    n_cells    = n(),
    pct_tumor  = 100 * mean(metacluster == "tumor"),
    het_tumor  = shannon(table(droplevels(celltype[metacluster == "tumor"]))),
    het_immune = shannon(table(droplevels(celltype[metacluster %in% immune_meta]))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
ctrl <- samples$timepoint == "control"
samples[ctrl, c("mycn", "loss1p", "prog")] <- NA   # not applicable to the controls
rownames(samples) <- samples$fm_id

tp_levels <- intersect(TIMEPOINT_LEVELS, unique(samples$timepoint))
samples$timepoint <- factor(samples$timepoint, levels = tp_levels)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(timepoint = samples$timepoint), responseName = "n_samples"))
```

## Clustering input

As in MapMetSC, per-sample proportions are compositional, so we add a per-sample pseudocount (`CLR_PSEUDO` cells / cells of the sample) and apply a centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation; the samples are then clustered hierarchically with **Euclidean distance and Ward.D2 linkage** (`hclust(method = "ward.D2")`).

```{r clr}
set.seed(20231103)

distance   <- "euclidean"
linkage    <- "ward.D2"
CLR_PSEUDO <- 0.5

clust_cells <- if (!is.null(clust_meta)) cells[cells$metacluster %in% clust_meta, ] else cells
counts_ct <- as.matrix(table(factor(clust_cells$fm_id, levels = samples$fm_id), droplevels(clust_cells$celltype)))
counts_ct <- counts_ct[, colSums(counts_ct) > 0, drop = FALSE]
prop_ct   <- counts_ct / rowSums(counts_ct)
cmat_adj  <- sweep(prop_ct, 1, CLR_PSEUDO / rowSums(counts_ct), "+")
clr_df    <- t(apply(cmat_adj, 1, function(x) log(x) - mean(log(x))))

dist_matrix <- dist(clr_df, method = distance)
hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = linkage)
```

## Number of communities

Three criteria for the number of communities k, all computed on the same CLR distance and Ward.D2 tree:

* **average silhouette width** ([Rousseeuw 1987](https://doi.org/10.1016/0377-0427(87)90125-7)): how much closer samples are to their own community than to the nearest other one (higher is better);
* **gap statistic** ([Tibshirani et al. 2001](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9868.00293)): within-community dispersion compared with uniform reference data; the k chosen with the "first SE max" rule;
* **bootstrap stability** ([Hennig 2007](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csda.2006.11.025)): the samples are resampled `r params$n_boot` times and re-clustered; for each community, the mean Jaccard similarity with its best-matching bootstrap community. Hennig's guide: < 0.6 the community dissolves, ≥ 0.75 it is stable. The plot shows the least stable community of each k.

At least 2 communities are always cut. `n_communities = "auto"` takes the largest k whose least stable community still has a mean bootstrap Jaccard ≥ 0.75 (every community stable), and the gap-statistic k if no k passes; otherwise `n_communities` is used as set (`r params$n_communities` here). The average silhouette width tends to favour k = 2 when one group of samples is very distinct, so it is reported but not used for the choice.

```{r choose-k, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}
k_range  <- 2:max(2, min(params$k_max, nrow(clr_df) - 1))
hc_cut   <- function(x, k) list(cluster = cutree(hclust(dist(x, method = distance), method = linkage), k))

sil_width <- vapply(k_range, function(k)
  mean(silhouette(cutree(hc, k), dist_matrix)[, "sil_width"]), numeric(1))

set.seed(20231103)
gap    <- clusGap(clr_df, FUNcluster = hc_cut, K.max = max(k_range), B = params$n_boot, verbose = FALSE)
gap_k  <- max(2, maxSE(gap$Tab[, "gap"], gap$Tab[, "SE.sim"], method = "firstSEmax"))   # at least 2 communities

# Bootstrap stability (clusterwise Jaccard, as fpc::clusterboot)
set.seed(20231103)
n_s  <- nrow(clr_df)
jacc <- lapply(k_range, function(k) matrix(NA_real_, params$n_boot, k))
for (b in seq_len(params$n_boot)) {
  idx  <- sample(n_s, n_s, replace = TRUE)
  hc_b <- hclust(dist(clr_df[idx, , drop = FALSE], method = distance), method = linkage)
  u    <- !duplicated(idx)
  for (i in seq_along(k_range)) {
    k    <- k_range[i]
    cl_b <- cutree(hc_b, k)[u]
    cl_o <- cutree(hc, k)[idx[u]]
    for (c0 in seq_len(k)) {
      in0 <- cl_o == c0
      if (!any(in0)) next
      jacc[[i]][b, c0] <- max(vapply(unique(cl_b), function(c1) {
        in1 <- cl_b == c1; sum(in0 & in1) / sum(in0 | in1) }, numeric(1)))
    }
  }
}
```

```{r choose-k-table, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}
stab_min  <- vapply(jacc, function(m) min(colMeans(m, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
stab_mean <- vapply(jacc, function(m) mean(colMeans(m, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
k_diag <- data.frame(k = k_range, silhouette = sil_width, gap = gap$Tab[k_range, "gap"],
                     gap_SE = gap$Tab[k_range, "SE.sim"],
                     jaccard_min = stab_min, jaccard_mean = stab_mean)
sil_k  <- k_range[which.max(sil_width)]
stab_k <- if (any(stab_min >= 0.75)) max(k_range[stab_min >= 0.75]) else gap_k
knitr::kable(k_diag, digits = 3,
             caption = paste0("Best k: bootstrap stability (largest k with all Jaccard >= 0.75) = ", stab_k,
                              ", gap statistic (firstSEmax) = ", gap_k, ", silhouette = ", sil_k))
write.csv(k_diag, file.path(plot_dir, paste0(date_prefix, "_n_communities_criteria.csv")), row.names = FALSE)

n_comm <- if (identical(as.character(params$n_communities), "auto")) stab_k else as.integer(params$n_communities)
n_comm <- max(2L, as.integer(n_comm))   # at least 2 communities
message("[05.1 ", variant, "] k: stability = ", stab_k, ", gap = ", gap_k, ", silhouette = ", sil_k, "; using ", n_comm)

k_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(k = k_range, value = sil_width, criterion = "average silhouette width"),
  data.frame(k = k_range, value = k_diag$gap, criterion = "gap statistic"),
  data.frame(k = k_range, value = stab_min, criterion = "bootstrap Jaccard (least stable community)"))
k_long$criterion <- factor(k_long$criterion, levels = unique(k_long$criterion))
p_k <- ggplot(k_long, aes(k, value)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n_comm, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(criterion = factor("bootstrap Jaccard (least stable community)", levels = levels(k_long$criterion)),
                               y = c(0.6, 0.75)), aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~ criterion, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) +
  labs(y = NULL, subtitle = paste0("dashed: k used (", n_comm, ")")) +
  theme_bw()
p_k
save_plot(p_k, "n_communities_criteria.pdf", width = 12, height = 4)
```

## Cluster cellular communities

The dendrogram is cut into `r n_comm` communities, numbered by size (community 1 is the largest).

```{r cluster-communities}
# Reorder leaves so the larger community sorts to the left (branch swaps only)
comm_membership   <- cutree(hc, k = n_comm)
comm_sizes        <- table(comm_membership)
comm_rank_by_size <- rank(-as.integer(comm_sizes), ties.method = "first")
names(comm_rank_by_size) <- names(comm_sizes)
hc <- as.hclust(reorder(as.dendrogram(hc), wts = unname(comm_rank_by_size[as.character(comm_membership)]),
                        agglo.FUN = mean))

# Community numbers by size: the largest is community 1
samples$community <- factor(unname(comm_rank_by_size[as.character(cutree(hc, k = n_comm)[samples$fm_id])]))
clustered_samples <- rownames(clr_df)[hc$order]
community_levels  <- levels(samples$community)
community_palette <- setNames(viridisLite::viridis(max(8, length(community_levels)))[seq_along(community_levels)],
                              community_levels)

knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(community = samples$community, timepoint = samples$timepoint)),
             caption = "Samples per community and BM sample type")
```

We save each sample's community with its metadata for the downstream analyses (05.2).

```{r save-communities}
out_tab <- samples[clustered_samples, ]
out_tab$cluster_on <- params$cluster_on
write.csv(out_tab, file.path(params$output, paste0("communities_BM_", variant, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(out_tab, file.path(params$output, paste0("communities_BM_", variant, ".rds")))
```

p_dend_plain <- ggdendrogram(hc, labels = length(clustered_samples) <= 80) +
  ggtitle(paste0("Samples clustered on ", params$cluster_on, " cell types (CLR, ", distance, ", ", linkage, ")"))
p_dend_plain
save_plot(p_dend_plain, "dendrogram.pdf", width = 10, height = 6)

## Summary statistics per community

Discrete sample metadata per community (pie charts) - the BM sample type and the patient-level MYCN amplification, 1p loss and progression (not applicable to the controls):

```{r piecharts, fig.height=8, fig.width=7}
pie_vars <- list(timepoint = list(title = "BM sample", cols = COL_TIMEPOINT),
                 mycn      = list(title = "MYCN amp.", cols = COL_YNH),
                 loss1p    = list(title = "1p loss",   cols = COL_YNH),
                 prog      = list(title = "progression", cols = COL_YNH))
pie_list <- lapply(names(pie_vars), function(v) {
  d <- samples[!is.na(samples[[v]]), ] %>% count(community, value = as.character(.data[[v]]))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = value)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill") +
    coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
    facet_grid(. ~ community) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pie_vars[[v]]$cols, name = pie_vars[[v]]$title) +
    theme_void()
})
p_pie <- wrap_plots(pie_list, ncol = 1)
p_pie
save_plot(p_pie, "piecharts_metadata.pdf", width = 7, height = 8)
```

Continuous sample metadata per community (Kruskal-Wallis p-value in each title): the tumor-cell fraction, the tumor and immune heterogeneity (Shannon entropy of the cell-type composition within the compartment) and the age at diagnosis.

```{r boxplots, fig.height=4, fig.width=12}
cont_vars <- c(pct_tumor = "% tumor cells", het_tumor = "tumor heterogeneity",
               het_immune = "immune heterogeneity", age_diag = "age at diagnosis [months]")
box_list <- lapply(names(cont_vars), function(v) {
  d <- samples[!is.na(samples[[v]]), ]
  p_kw <- if (length(unique(d$community)) > 1) signif(kruskal.test(d[[v]] ~ d$community)$p.value, 2) else NA
  ggplot(d, aes(community, .data[[v]], fill = community)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = community_palette, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0(cont_vars[[v]], "\np = ", p_kw), x = "community", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
})
p_box <- wrap_plots(box_list, nrow = 1)
p_box
save_plot(p_box, "boxplots_metadata.pdf", width = 12, height = 4)
```

## Combined figures (stacked panels)

As in MapMetSC's Fig 3a, the panels share one sample order, with a blank spacer column between sample groups: dendrogram, the composition used for the clustering, BM sample type, community and genetic / clinical tracks, tumor cell types (within the tumor cells), immune cell types (within the immune cells) and metaclusters. Legends are laid out in two columns.

* `combined_stacked.pdf`: samples in dendrogram order, grouped by community;
* `combined_stacked_by_timepoint.pdf`: samples grouped by BM sample type (`r paste(tp_levels, collapse = " / ")`) and, within each group, ordered by their own clustering (same CLR distance and Ward.D2 linkage, one dendrogram per group).

```{r stacked-helpers}
X_EXPAND <- expansion(add = 0.5)
LEG2 <- guide_legend(ncol = 2)

# ordered: sample ids in plotting order; group: group label per ordered sample;
# segs: dendrogram segments on the 1..N sample axis (or NULL)
stacked_figure <- function(ordered, group, segs, top_title, clustering_title) {
  N <- length(ordered)
  boundary_idx <- which(group[-1] != group[-N])
  lev_spaced <- ordered
  for (b in rev(seq_along(boundary_idx)))
    lev_spaced <- append(lev_spaced, paste0("__gap__", b), after = boundary_idx[b])
  M        <- length(lev_spaced)
  remap_x  <- function(v) v + vapply(v, function(z) sum(boundary_idx < z), numeric(1))
  real_pos <- remap_x(seq_len(N))

  # ---- top panel: dendrogram(s) and group labels ----
  grp_lev <- unique(group)
  h_root  <- if (!is.null(segs) && nrow(segs)) max(c(segs$y, segs$yend)) else 1
  lab_df  <- data.frame(x = vapply(grp_lev, function(g) mean(real_pos[group == g]), numeric(1)),
                        y = h_root * 1.08, label = grp_lev)
  p_top <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(data = lab_df, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label), fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, M + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, h_root * 1.15), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = top_title) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0.5), plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 0, 2))
  if (!is.null(segs) && nrow(segs)) {
    segs$x <- remap_x(segs$x); segs$xend <- remap_x(segs$xend)
    p_top <- p_top + geom_segment(data = segs, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend))
  }

  # ---- composition barplots (% of the cells in the panel's subset) ----
  comp_bar <- function(d, var, cols, legend_title) {
    tab <- d %>% count(fm_id, value = .data[[var]]) %>%
      group_by(fm_id) %>% mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
      mutate(fm_id = factor(fm_id, levels = lev_spaced))
    ggplot(tab, aes(fm_id, pct, fill = value)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.9) +
      scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, expand = X_EXPAND) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = legend_title, drop = TRUE, guide = LEG2) +
      labs(y = "%") +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank(),
            axis.line.x = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2))
  }
  cells_k  <- cells[cells$fm_id %in% ordered, ]
  p_clust  <- comp_bar(if (!is.null(clust_meta)) cells_k[cells_k$metacluster %in% clust_meta, ] else cells_k,
                       "celltype", col_celltype, clustering_title)
  p_all    <- comp_bar(cells_k, "celltype", col_celltype, "All cell types")
  p_tumor  <- comp_bar(cells_k[cells_k$metacluster == "tumor", ], "celltype", col_celltype, "Tumor cell types")
  p_immune <- comp_bar(cells_k[cells_k$metacluster %in% immune_meta, ], "celltype", col_celltype, "Immune cell types")
  p_meta   <- comp_bar(cells_k, "metacluster", col_metacluster, "Metaclusters")

  # ---- metadata strips ----
  meta_df <- samples[ordered, ]
  meta_df$fm_id <- factor(meta_df$fm_id, levels = lev_spaced)
  strip <- function(var, cols, name) {
    ggplot(meta_df, aes(fm_id, 1, fill = as.character(.data[[var]]))) +
      geom_tile() +
      scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, expand = X_EXPAND) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = name, na.value = "white", guide = LEG2) +
      labs(y = name) +
      theme_void() +
      theme(axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
            plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2))
  }
  # continuous tracks (as in the age / TU het. / ME het. rows of published BM figures)
  strip_cont <- function(var, name, option) {
    ggplot(meta_df, aes(fm_id, 1, fill = .data[[var]])) +
      geom_tile() +
      scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, expand = X_EXPAND) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(option = option, name = name, na.value = "white",
                           guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top",
                                                   barheight = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"))) +
      labs(y = name) +
      theme_void() +
      theme(axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
            plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2))
  }
  strips <- list(strip("timepoint", COL_TIMEPOINT, "BM sample"),
                 strip("community", community_palette, "community"),
                 strip("mycn",   COL_YNH, "MYCN amp."),
                 strip("loss1p", COL_YNH, "1p loss"),
                 strip("prog",   COL_YNH, "progression"),
                 strip_cont("age_diag",   "age [months]", "magma"),
                 strip_cont("het_tumor",  "TU het.",      "viridis"),
                 strip_cont("het_immune", "immune het.",  "cividis"))

  # Same number of panels in every variant: clustered on all cell types, the
  # clustering panel is the all-cell-type panel (+ immune panel); clustered on
  # immune / T-cell types, the all-cell-type panel replaces the immune panel.
  panels  <- c(list(p_top, p_clust), strips,
               if (params$cluster_on == "all") list(p_tumor, p_immune) else list(p_all, p_tumor),
               list(p_meta))
  heights <- c(2, 4, rep(0.3, length(strips)), 3, 3, 3)
  wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 1) + plot_layout(heights = heights, guides = "collect")
}
fig_width  <- function(M) max(14, 8 + 0.05 * M)   # wider for the two-column legends
clust_title <- c(all = "All cell types (clustering)", immune = "Immune cell types (clustering)",
                 tcell = "T-cell types (clustering)")[[params$cluster_on]]
```

```{r combined-figure, fig.width=18, fig.height=15}
segs <- segment(dendro_data(hc, type = "rectangle"))
p_combined <- stacked_figure(clustered_samples, as.character(samples[clustered_samples, "community"]),
                             segs, "Community", clust_title)
p_combined
save_plot(p_combined, "combined_stacked.pdf", width = fig_width(length(clustered_samples)), height = 15)
```

```{r combined-figure-by-timepoint, fig.width=18, fig.height=15}
# Within each BM sample type: own Ward.D2 clustering on the same CLR values
ord_tp <- character(0); segs_tp <- NULL; offset <- 0
for (tp in tp_levels) {
  ids <- samples$fm_id[samples$timepoint == tp]
  ids <- ids[ids %in% rownames(clr_df)]
  if (length(ids) >= 2) {
    hc_tp <- hclust(dist(clr_df[ids, , drop = FALSE], method = distance), method = linkage)
    s_tp  <- segment(dendro_data(hc_tp, type = "rectangle"))
    s_tp$x <- s_tp$x + offset; s_tp$xend <- s_tp$xend + offset
    segs_tp <- rbind(segs_tp, s_tp)
    ids <- ids[hc_tp$order]
  }
  ord_tp <- c(ord_tp, ids); offset <- offset + length(ids)
}
p_combined_tp <- stacked_figure(ord_tp, as.character(samples[ord_tp, "timepoint"]),
                                segs_tp, "BM sample", clust_title)
p_combined_tp
save_plot(p_combined_tp, "combined_stacked_by_timepoint.pdf", width = fig_width(length(ord_tp)), height = 15)
```
